REQ-438|pass.note: No temporary or emergency account in the controller store carried an expiry more than seventy-two hours past its creation stamp, and the expired accounts were present and disabled rather than absent, which keeps their history available to an investigation. REQ-439|pass.note: Every disable record in the sample carried exactly one of the three trigger codes — expiry, loss of programme association, or a recorded policy violation — and each interval from trigger to disable came in under the seventy-two hour bound. REQ-440|pass.note: Thirty consecutive daily sweep runs appear in the log with no gap, and no enabled ground support account carried a last-successful-authentication stamp older than ninety days. REQ-441|pass.note: Every account action in the thirty-day sample paired to an audit record naming the actor, the target account, the action and the authorising role, each with its write receipt from the storage module attached. REQ-446|not-assessed.note: The analytics design record defines the three pattern dimensions and their thresholds and the correlation rule set has a dated build item with a named owner, but no rule is fielded and no atypical-usage alert has ever been raised, so the examination would have compared a design against nothing running.

REQ-449|fail.note: All three approved tunnels were presented to the inspection path in cleartext before release, and an encrypted flow whose key the cryptographic module does not hold was blocked at the boundary rather than passed uninspected. REQ-450|pass.note: The enumerated security function list on the mission computer matched the approved list item for item, and the cryptographic module refused a key operation presented with a role not named for that function even though the calling service had already authorised it. REQ-451|pass.note: The design record shows privileged and non-privileged accounts issued in one transaction, so a privileged role cannot exist without the everyday account that keeps it out of nonsecurity work, and the mission computer refuses to open mission planning, telemetry review or documentation under a privileged role. REQ-452|pass.note: A privileged command was offered on every gateway interface in turn and dropped on all but the single approved maintenance path, with each drop logged; the approved privileged path list holds exactly one entry. REQ-453|pass.note: Every privileged role holder on both components reconciled to an entry on the current approved privileged-personnel list, with no holder carried over from a superseded list. REQ-454|fail.note: The worksheet is genuinely evidence-led — each holder's assignment sits beside their preceding 180 days of privileged activity drawn from the collector, and the reviewer signed reconfirmation decisions against that rather than against the role names. REQ-456|pass.note: Ten successful and ten denied privileged executions each produced a record at the collector naming the function, the role, the account and the outcome, with the denial path carrying the same four fields as the success path so a run of refused calls is as visible as a run of accepted ones. REQ-457|pass.note: Privileged calls attempted from a non-privileged session were refused on every path into the mission computer, including through the mission scripting interface, where the check happens at dispatch so a privileged call cannot be smuggled through a data argument. REQ-458|pass.note: A fourth concurrent session was refused on both terminators for every account type tested, privileged and service accounts included, and the refusal named the concurrent session limit as its reason rather than returning a generic error. REQ-459|pass.note: Frame captures at lock showed an opaque surface with no mission data, no account name and no window title readable on either station, including on an external display attached to the laptop during maintenance. REQ-460|pass.note: The logout action was reachable from every authenticated screen on both stations, and taking it closed the downstream maintenance sessions the session had opened on three other LRUs, matched by session identifier rather than by timeout. REQ-461|pass.note: Each of the three termination causes produced its own on-screen message on both stations, so a technician returning to a station can tell an idle timeout from an administrator cutting the session rather than guessing from an empty screen. REQ-464|not-assessed.note: Attribute carriage across the gateway and the internal transport is scheduled for the 4.4 build and neither the on-the-wire encoding nor the drop behaviour for an unmarked object exists outside the design intent, so no object crossing either component carries an attribute today.

REQ-466|not-assessed.note: The dictionary format is approved and its distribution rides the existing signed configuration path, but nothing has been issued to any of the three LRUs, so there is no versioned artefact to examine and no fielded halt behaviour to compare a design record against.

REQ-467|pass.note: Session start appeared at the collector inside the ten second bound on all six sampled sessions, and commands issued during a session showed up while it was still open rather than after it closed, which is what makes the disconnect action usable. REQ-468|pass.note: No remote maintenance traffic was observable in cleartext on the gateway external interface, and the post-session storage sweep found no residual session key material on the gateway itself, so recovering that unit yields nothing with which to replay a captured session. REQ-469|pass.note: The approved network baseline shows exactly one external remote access path — the boundary gateway forwarding to the maintenance gateway — and the release boundary scan found no externally reachable listening remote access service on any other LRU. REQ-470|fail.note: A command absent from the approved remote-privileged list was refused with its reason code, and a laptop failing device attestation could not open a privileged session at all; both refusals are present in the session log. The third check is not a check: an out-of-window privileged command was logged and then admitted, so the scheduled maintenance window bounds the record rather than the access, and two of the three admission conditions the requirement states are enforced.

REQ-470|pass.note: Revisited once the window check was made binding. A privileged command offered outside the scheduled maintenance window was refused with its reason code rather than logged and admitted, so all three admission conditions now gate the command instead of two gating it and one describing it. REQ-474|inconclusive.note: Commands carrying invalid authentication tags were discarded at the radio and the payload command case was discarded again at the interface controller, and both discard counters were readable in the maintenance download. REQ-477|pass.note: Every enrolled laptop reported full-device encryption enabled with the key bound to platform hardware rather than to a user passphrase, and a non-compliant unit is refused at connection rather than merely flagged for follow-up. Storage lifted from a powered-off laptop and read on a second host yielded no readable programme data.

REQ-480|not-assessed.note: Neither store applies a query rate ceiling, a per-role extraction volume limit or an alert on a sequential full-set read, and the technique set that would define those values is still a draft, so an authorised account can enumerate a whole store today and there is nothing fielded for an examination to measure.

REQ-481|pass.note: The policy and every procedure artifact carried a valid signature and a review date inside twelve months, and aging one artifact past that boundary in test raised the repository's staleness flag as designed. REQ-484|pass.note: Re-running the repository query reproduced the critical asset list byte for byte, which is the property that matters here: the list is generated from the designations rather than kept alongside them. REQ-486|fail.note: Two exercise records exist inside the seven month spacing and each carries a measured duration, and every partition that was restored passed its integrity check on read-out. REQ-488|pass.note: The storage and retrieval agreement is signed and names a custodian, a release approver and a maximum retrieval time, and the rehearsal returned a usable backup set and a usable baseline set inside that time rather than merely proving the media were readable. The alternate facility's access approval and handling rules were produced and read alongside the primary's during the walkthrough; the formal line-by-line comparison remains an outstanding programme record and was noted as such.

REQ-490|not-assessed.note: No obstacle list has been written for any access route to the alternate facility, the media release authorisation still names an organisation rather than a role, and no retrieval walkthrough has been rehearsed, so the sequence could not have been described without reading from an unpublished note.

REQ-492|not-assessed.note: The candidate facility has been surveyed and draws power and network entry from different providers with its own badge system, but none of that is recorded in the contingency plan, the threat set the separation is meant to decorrelate is unstated, and the independent-entry confirmation is unsigned, so the alternate build remains nominated rather than assured.

REQ-495|not-assessed.note: The list of operations the contingency plan treats as essential has not been baselined, bearer-loss detection is a manual call today, and no failover has ever been timed, so there was no resumption measurement to take and nothing to observe about suppression of non-essential traffic.

REQ-498|fail.note: Both traces were built from live interface and routing state rather than from a drawing, and carrier-side disjointness holds — different transmission lines and different points of presence on the primary and alternate services. The trace fails by its own rule on the platform: the same internal switch port group appears on both paths, which is exactly the shared element the requirement forbids, and re-homing the radio path onto a separate group is still open.

REQ-499|pass.note: Three consecutive monthly cycles are recorded with no gap approaching thirty-one days, each naming the partition selected at random for the scratch restore and reporting its integrity result rather than a bare pass. An induced hash mismatch raised the maintenance alert and the alert was still present after a controller restart, and it could not be cleared without a subsequent passing verification.

REQ-501|pass.note: A raw read of the backup partition returned no plaintext configuration or audit string under inspection, and an attempt to seal a set with the integrity tag suppressed was refused and logged rather than completing with a missing tag. Altering a single byte of an already sealed set caused the tag check to fail at the next verification, so the seal is a property of the content and not a flag on the record.

REQ-502|pass.note: No interface on the module returned a backup key in cleartext under any of the export attempts made, and a wrap request presented under a maintenance role identity was rejected and logged with the requesting identity attached. Key generation events each carried the role identity that asked for them, so the storage role's exclusive use of the backup wrap path is demonstrable from the module's own record rather than from configuration alone.

REQ-503|pass.note: Cutting power during a staged update left the platform booting the previous known-good image with the partial transaction discarded in the journal rather than marked complete. The post-recovery attestation from the boot controller was recorded and compared against the intended image digest before the transaction was allowed to close, so completion follows what actually booted rather than what was staged.

REQ-505|pass.note: Every artifact in the set carried a named approver and a review date inside twelve months, and an artifact whose review date was deliberately aged past that point in test was flagged by the repository without anyone raising it. Each published revision carried the publishing operator's identity and a diff against its predecessor, so a change to a procedure is attributable to a person and readable as a change rather than as a new document.

REQ-506|pass.note: The assessor role definition grants read of configuration and health state and no write, clear or approve permission anywhere in the set, and no account was found holding an assessor role and an engineering role at the same time. An export of the correlated record set taken under that role succeeded and was itself written as an access event attributable to the assessor identity, so independence is enforced by the access model rather than asserted in a plan.

REQ-507|not-assessed.note: The assessment plan carries no specialised-assessment frequency, no determination has been made about which activity is announced, and no rules of engagement exist for the malicious-user exercise, so neither activity could have been run and neither result exists in any form.

REQ-508|fail.note: Every exchange enabled in the gateway policy set reports an agreement identifier, and the tactical data link agreement is signed, current and records the impact level and control responsibilities on both sides. The ground-support telemetry exchange is the exception that matters: it is live today under a time-bounded interim approval with its agreement still in draft, so an exchange is carrying information across the boundary without the signed agreement the requirement makes a precondition of enabling it.

REQ-509|pass.note: A write offered from an identity with no recorded authorization was rejected at the boundary and logged with the identity and destination, and a write from an authorized identity aimed at a data set outside its authorization was rejected on the same basis. The outbound telemetry path still releases on link-layer identity rather than a recorded read authorization; that direction was noted beside the result as the open half of the control.

REQ-513|not-assessed.note: The monitoring dataset carries a compliance result only: no effectiveness measure is defined for any control family and the change view is not joined to repository commits, so there is no three-view dataset in which a degradation could be told apart from a drift and nothing for the examination to open.

REQ-515|pass.note: Every presented monitoring result carried the time it was produced with a stale flag computed from it, so an old pass reads as old rather than as current. Suppressing the controller feed for twenty minutes raised the collection alarm inside the fifteen minute rule, and the assessor regenerated the presented dataset from the collector on demand, confirming nothing in it had been assembled by hand.

REQ-516|pass.note: The test team roster contains no individual holding a build or operate role on either the boundary gateway or the maintenance gateway, and the rules of engagement are dated before the first test activity rather than written up alongside the report. The report lists every attempted technique with its outcome, including those that did not succeed, which is what makes the coverage of the test assessable and not just its findings.

REQ-518|pass.note: Connecting an unregistered endpoint left the switch port unforwarding and raised a register-mismatch event naming the port and the endpoint, and every register entry read carried both interface characteristics and the nature of the data the connection carries. The sensor connections aggregated on the navigation side are described in the register but not yet enforced against it, and the review record for the expanded register is outstanding; both were logged against the next cycle.

REQ-520|not-assessed.note: WS-X90 has no system-level risk assessment policy of its own — the annual review parameter is met at enterprise level only — so the repository holds no signed set to examine, no revision names a designated risk-assessment official, and the staleness flag that would block promotion of a release package does not exist.

REQ-521|pass.note: The categorization record states confidentiality high, integrity high and availability moderate with a separate impact rationale for each objective and a dated authorizing official approval on the current revision. An artifact exported by the mission computer carried a categorization label byte-identical to the record value, so a downstream consumer reads the categorization off the artifact instead of having to look it up or infer it.

REQ-524|not-assessed.note: The platform holds no representation of the current threat environment: boundary policy is static between baselines, the state machine and the per-state policy set are unbuilt, and no bulletin ingest exists, so there was no threat state with a refresh timestamp to read and no second policy to compare against the first.

REQ-525|fail.note: Scans started on signature sets aged six and twenty-three hours ran as expected and the operator alert text is in place. The enforcement is not: the run started on a thirty-hour-old set completed normally instead of aborting, so the twenty-four hour window exists as a schedule rather than as a gate, and the signature set identifier appears in the scan log but not in the report header a reviewer actually reads.

REQ-528|pass.note: A credentialed scan of the mission computer baseline succeeded inside an authorized window and was refused to a laptop session that did not hold the privileged scan role, with the refusal written to the gateway audit stream against the requesting session identity. Repeating the scan on the same connection after session teardown failed, confirming the role is revoked as part of the teardown rather than left standing on the endpoint until it expires.

REQ-530|not-assessed.note: Aurora operates no publicly reachable reporting address for WS-X90 components and no intake register has been specified, so reports arriving by other routes are still worked case by case with no receipt commitment and no recorded decision authority for a triage path to be walked through.

REQ-531|inconclusive.note: Each finding carried from the completed assessment has a response decision in the register, with an accepting authority on every acceptance and a POA&M item on every mitigation, so the practice itself is visible. The determination could not be closed on the timing: the register extract stops at 20 October and the fifteen working day clock is kept in a separate spreadsheet that was not produced, so the assessor could not establish whether any decision was late.

REQ-532|pass.note: The three functions the requirement names — the navigation integrity monitor, the interlock arm and inhibit path and the root-of-trust verification — are each classified mission-critical with a named protection allocation, and the analysis revision follows the most recent baseline change board. The ground support functions still carry no classification and one of the three supply chain measures columns is empty; both were recorded as observations against a baseline 4.2 analysis that otherwise does what the requirement asks.

REQ-535|not-assessed.note: No WS-X90-specific literacy content exists and no account gate reads a completion date, so the population that would deliver and record the training is not yet stood up and there was nobody to interview about a course that has not been written.

REQ-538|not-assessed.note: No anomalous-behaviour indicator set has been published, so operators are still trained on generic guidance that does not map to the plausibility rejects, out-of-envelope health values and alert classes this platform actually produces, and there was no published set against which a sampled operator could have been asked to classify anything.

REQ-540|not-assessed.note: No threat bulletin has been issued in any quarter: threat information reaches the engineering team and stops there, and no revision of the operating instructions cross-references a bulletin, so an operator could not have been asked which threat theme is current.

REQ-545|pass.note: Every WS-X90 account holder resolved to a training record carrying the course and completion date, and records for closed accounts were still retrievable across the three-year retention window rather than being purged at closure. Expiry is derived by hand from the course cadence instead of being held as a field, and the gates read a date at enablement rather than a published status; the assessor recorded both against an otherwise complete register.

REQ-546|not-assessed.note: Training completion for WS-X90 personnel is recorded and read by nobody: no report has gone to a supervisor or to the cybersecurity official in the last twelve months, so there was no reporting practice to discuss and no filed report to test the individual-failure requirement against.

REQ-550|not-assessed.note: Operating intent for WS-X90 is still spread across the security plan and the maintenance procedures with no concept of operations written, so there is no document naming a decision authority per mission phase and nothing stating the controlled abort and recover posture the platform actually implements.

REQ-551|pass.note: Issue 5 is dated inside twelve months and no earlier than the last change to the external interface set, and for the subsystems it covers it separates functions carried from functions inherited rather than listing everything as provided. Two subsystems have no lists yet and no external dependency records an assumption or an owner for it; the assessor took the description as meeting the requirement for the scope it claims and carried the remainder forward as an observation.

REQ-557|pass.note: One selected baseline is recorded for the system, naming SP 800-53B High as its starting point and tying that choice to the recorded high water mark of the categorization values rather than asserting it. Every control in the resulting set carries an entry in the selection trail, so the baseline reads as a derivation with an order to it and no control appears without a reason for being there.

REQ-558|pass.note: Replaying the recorded tailoring events over SP 800-53B High reproduced the effective control set exactly, which is the property that makes the difference between the published baseline and what the platform carries reconstructible without anyone's recollection. Every event named a control, an action, a driver and an approving authority, and a control introduced without a matching event was rejected at baseline review with the rejection recorded.

REQ-559|fail.note: The policy and the seven procedures that supported the original scope are signed, version-tagged and bound to the named configuration management official, the repository computes the review-overdue flag as designed, and the dissemination list for revision 4.0 covers each engineering and cybersecurity role in the policy. Four of the eleven procedures are not signed at all: those covering automated change prohibition, automated security response, information location and signed components are drafts, and the repository already reports them review-overdue, so the artifact set the requirement asks for is four procedures short of existing.

REQ-560|pass.note: A seeded firmware version change on a monitored LRU reached the baseline record in six minutes forty-one seconds with nobody typing it in, and the record carried the stale marker between the observed change and the completed reconciliation rather than jumping straight to the new value. The reconciliation entry recorded the prior value, the observed value and the source LRU, which is what lets an unexpected change be read as a change rather than as a correction.

REQ-561|pass.note: Every baseline in the repository holds at least two prior approved versions and each of their original approval signatures verified under the weekly sweep. The rollback exercise applied the second-most-recent retained version through the recovery controller using repository content alone, reaching for nothing outside it, and a deliberately tampered retained version came back as a retention integrity fault rather than disappearing from the set.

REQ-562|not-assessed.note: The reduced travel image and the issue and return record schema are drafted but neither is in use, and the gate that would stop a returned laptop opening a maintenance session before re-image and re-enrolment does not exist, so the return step is still a procedural instruction and there were no travel records to sample.

REQ-563|inconclusive.note: An unapproved change artifact was refused for staging at the repository and rejected again at the controller for carrying no released change record identifier, so both enforcement points behave as described. The remaining behaviours could not be exercised: the aging highlight for records left undecided beyond ten working days is only surfaced in a weekly report that did not fall inside the test window, and no completion notification could be observed, so the determination is left open.

REQ-564|pass.note: Every change record applied in the quarter carried a completed test result, a validation statement and the identity of the engineer who signed it, and the statements named the specific controls examined rather than asserting compliance in general. A package whose record was missing one of the three was held in the staging area and reported as an incomplete record instead of being applied and corrected later.

REQ-567|pass.note: The repository register carries the algorithm suite, key strength, trust anchor set and module firmware version for both the cryptographic module and the radio as configuration items, and the cross-reference resolves every crypto-dependent control in the tailored set to at least one of them. An attempt to change an algorithm suite from an operational console was refused and logged, so a waveform crypto change is a board decision rather than an operator setting.

REQ-568|fail.note: Three monthly reconciliation cycles are complete and the output separates applied-without-record from record-without-applied rather than merging them, and a post-incident review was run after the August integration incident. What the interviews established is that nobody owns the event-driven leg: the roles gave different accounts of who authorises a review once a planned change campaign completes, there is no trigger that opens one, and on that leg accountability is not established at all.

REQ-569|not-assessed.note: The platform state signal exists but neither refusal has been built: the controller will still apply a configuration change while the platform reports an exercise or operational state, and the interlock has no independent block of its own, so submitting a change in the rig would have demonstrated nothing about the control.

REQ-572|pass.note: A user outside the authorised change role list was denied both a repository write and a change action offered through a maintenance session, and each denial produced an audit record at the collector naming the actor, the object and the decision — as did the permitted action. Thirty days of enforcement records contain no path to a released artifact that reaches it without passing one of the two enforcement points.

REQ-573|pass.note: The responsible role walked through the grant path from the maintainer list to the honoured privilege and produced the signed re-evaluation record, which re-justifies each retained holder by name and shows two dormant holders withdrawn at the last cycle. The three integration engineers holding both the development and the operational change role do so under a recorded exception, which the account acknowledged carries no expiry date and is re-argued each cycle rather than closed.

REQ-574|pass.note: An interactive administrative account was refused a write to the mission software library at the filesystem enforcement point, before the write reached library contents, and each refusal produced a privilege violation record naming the attempting identity. The release pipeline identity completed a signed library update in the same run and the write was attributable to that identity alone, which is the whole of the permitted writer set.

REQ-575|pass.note: The verification pass covered every component the system record marks security-relevant, reaching into the navigation and timing subsystem rather than stopping at mission compute. A deliberately loosened navigation integrity threshold and an altered timing holdover setting were each reported by name at the next pass instead of being absorbed into a deviation count, and verification ran at bring-up and again inside the twenty-four hour window during sustained operation.

REQ-579|pass.note: An unapproved binary placed on the platform was refused at load and never reached an executing state, with the refusal record naming the image path and the computed measurement rather than a generic denial. The same refusal occurred with the platform in maintenance mode, so a mode switch does not relax the policy — the specific weakness this design set out to avoid.

REQ-581|pass.note: Every entry in the authorised software list names a program, its measurement and the mission function it supports, and the enforcement policy on both components is deny-all with that list as the only permit source. The most recent annual review removed four entries for having no current mission function, two of them development-era diagnostic utilities that had survived three baselines on the platform management side.

REQ-583|fail.note: An unlisted device was refused a maintenance session at the gateway and refused a data path on eight of the twelve switch ports, with each refusal reported inside thirty seconds naming the port and the presented device identity. Four ports fail it: they predate the enforcement firmware, so an unlisted device connecting there is detected and reported but still given a data path, which is a report rather than the admission control the requirement asks for.

REQ-583|pass.note: Returned to the twelve switch ports after remediation. The four that previously carried an advisory refusal now drop the data path on identity alone, and an unlisted device connected to each port in turn was refused and reported inside thirty seconds with the port and presented identity named. Behaviour on the maintenance port and the list review record were confirmed unchanged.

REQ-584|pass.note: The rehearsed replacement could not be closed until the inventory delta had been written and accepted, and the delta carried part number, serial number, firmware version and slot for both the removed and the installed unit rather than for the new one alone. An action closed without an accepted delta stayed open and was reported to the maintenance supervisor, which is what keeps the inventory from decaying quietly between formal audits.

REQ-585|pass.note: Daily inventory currency figures are retrievable for each of the last thirty operating days, computed only from automated observations, so no record reaches confirmed status on a manual entry. Records outside the twenty-four hour window are listed individually with the age of their last confirmation rather than absorbed into the percentage, which is what lets a persistent blind spot be told apart from a bad day.

REQ-586|pass.note: An unauthorised firmware image introduced between maintenance windows was detected without waiting for a scan, the affected function was isolated from the mission network, and the notification reached the collector in three minutes twelve seconds naming the measured value, the expected baseline value and the observing LRU. The payload interface controllers are still measured at bring-up rather than continuously, which the programme tracks separately and the assessor left outside this result.

REQ-591|pass.note: An installation attempted from an unelevated maintenance session was refused outright, and the elevation granted for the successful case expired at the end of its bounded window with no operator step to close it. Each installation record names the requesting identity, the elevation window and the package identifier, so the action ties to a person and a time-boxed grant rather than to a standing privilege on the laptop.

REQ-592|pass.note: Each protected information class resolves to a named set of components and a named set of roles able to reach it on each, and the rehearsed relocation produced a dated location-change record carrying a reason rather than a bare timestamp. No class is recorded as residing on a component absent from the system inventory, so the map and the inventory agree with one another.

REQ-594|not-assessed.note: The protected information type definitions exist but the discovery capability that would scan the exported data sets is not built and the exception record has no schema, so there is no scheduled run to evidence and nothing that could name a component, an information type and a detection basis.

REQ-595|pass.note: A firmware image signed by a certificate outside the approved set halted the affected LRU in its recovery state rather than continuing, and the recovery record named both the failing component and the certificate that had presented the signature. The command and configuration surfaces on the boot controller expose no setting that turns the check off, so verification cannot be relaxed from the operational platform.

REQ-596|pass.note: A package containing a single unsigned component was rejected in full at staging rather than being partially staged with the verifiable remainder, which is the behaviour that stops an update arriving half-trusted. Each component of the accepted control package recorded the certificate identity that verified it, so the provenance of a staged update can be reconstructed later, and no staging path was found that accepts a component without a signature check.

REQ-597|pass.note: Revision 2.4 came back with the System Security Engineer named as the designated official, a recorded review date against each artifact and no overdue flag standing anywhere in the set. Offering a revision from an endpoint outside the sole publication path produced a refusal in the repository event log rather than a second copy in circulation, and the recipient list bound to the published revision reaches every ground support and cybersecurity role holding an identification and authentication duty.

REQ-598|pass.note: A privileged login presenting only the PIN, and one presenting only the hardware credential, were each refused outright with no reduced-privilege session offered, and both refusals reached the security log inside five seconds carrying the credential serial and not the PIN. Key attestation shows the privileged authentication private key as non-exportable, and withdrawing the credential mid-session ended the session rather than letting queued commands run out.

REQ-599|fail.note: The provisioning workstation required a hardware credential and PIN on every path tested and offered no password-only method anywhere in its build configuration, and the laptop enforced the same pair whenever it was attached to the ground support network. Disconnected, it does not: a local password-only logon remains available on the flightline as an availability concession, so the endpoint that spends the most time away from the identity service is the one where the requirement is not met.

REQ-601|pass.note: The gateway required the separate hardware token on its local console, its network path and its remote support path for both account types, refused a pair of factors that both originated on the accessed endpoint, and dropped the session inside thirty seconds of the token being pulled. The laptop enforces the same on its network and remote paths; its local console still accepts two factors originating on the laptop, and the assessor recorded that residual path rather than treating the token mechanism as unimplemented.

REQ-602|pass.note: A captured privileged authentication exchange replayed against the gateway derived no session key and was refused under the replay-detected reason code, which appears as a distinct code in the exported security log rather than as a generic authentication failure. Each nonce in the radio's sortie session log appeared exactly once, and because the binding sits in the protocol rather than in an account policy the resistance covers every account type on both components.

REQ-603|inconclusive.note: A PIV credential that could not be chained to an accepted anchor was refused with no account binding, and a revoked credential was refused at the workstation with the revocation source named in the session record. The run stopped there: the harness lost telemetry from both endpoints before the indeterminate-status case could be driven against the laptop, which is the path where the disconnected revocation snapshot matters, so the determination waits on a rerun.

REQ-604|fail.note: A device presenting a valid certificate but a failed boot measurement was held in the quarantine VLAN, and mission traffic sourced from a port not in the authenticated state was dropped at the mission computer regardless of link status. The exchange is not mutual everywhere it claims to be: two attached devices completed the link without validating the certificate the switch presented, so on those ports the switch proves nothing to the device and only one direction of the authentication is real.

REQ-607|pass.note: A write to the attribute store offered from anything other than an authenticated controller channel was refused, and each accepted write appended an immutable revision record whose prior value matched what was read immediately before the change. The search for duplicate attribute copies after a provisioning cycle found none on the mission computer or the provisioning workstation, so the store really is single rather than nominally so.

REQ-608|pass.note: The compromised-password list held on the controller carries a September revision date, inside the three month window, and a refresh triggered by a compromise notification is recorded against that notification's reference. A password drawn from the list was rejected at the workstation with a generic message that names no entry, so the screening does not itself become a way to read the list.

REQ-609|fail.note: An eleven-character password and a twelve-character password missing a character class were both rejected, the credential path capture showed no plaintext on the wire, and a raw read of the credential region yielded only salt and derivation output. The change rule is not enforced everywhere: a change made through the controller's own reset path was accepted while leaving seven of twelve characters in position, so the at-least-half rule holds on the provisioning path and not on the other one.

REQ-610|pass.note: A certificate chaining to an unrecognised anchor was refused with a path-build failure recorded, and a certificate present in the cached revocation set was refused with no external link available at all. A cache aged past seven days was declared stale and the session refused rather than accepted on the assumption that nothing had changed, and an attempt to export the authentication private key returned a refusal and an audit record.

REQ-611|pass.note: The access control export for the credential region names the identity service principal and nothing else, and the key inventory records every authentication key as hardware-resident and non-exportable. Memory and storage images taken from the mission computer and the provisioning workstation contained no authenticator material, so the two permitted locations are in fact the only two.

REQ-615|pass.note: The manifest is signed and names every anchor with its purpose and expiry, and the radio's power-on digest matched the manifest digest of record; an anchor added outside the manifest raised a configuration deviation within a single power-on cycle. The telemetry unit reports its digest only during a maintenance download, so drift there surfaces a cycle late — carried as an observation rather than as a criterion failure, since the manifest itself governs both units.

REQ-616|not-assessed.note: Privileged credentials are issued in person by local practice, but the sponsor authorisation is captured on a separate form and is not bound to the credential serial in the provisioning record, so the binding cannot be verified from the system and there is no documented issuance sequence for the registration authority to walk through.

REQ-617|pass.note: Credential entry was masked on every surface of both endpoints including the recovery console, and a diagnostic capture taken straight after a failed logon contained none of the entered characters because they are never copied out of the input buffer. A failure against a valid identifier and one against an invalid identifier returned the identical message within the fifty millisecond timing bound, closing the latency channel that a masked display on its own leaves open.

REQ-618|pass.note: A keyed operation requested before role authentication returned a module status refusal rather than proceeding on the session alone, and a transition from the user role to the crypto officer role without re-authentication was refused. The storage module declined a key-wrapping request carrying no module role binding, which closes the path that would otherwise let the storage side be used to work around the role check.

REQ-622|pass.note: A connection attempt carrying only a device certificate was refused by all three services, and a service certificate whose subject did not match the hosting LRU inventory entry was refused as well, so a compromised but authenticated device cannot impersonate a service it does not host. Every accepted session recorded the peer service name and its hosting LRU in the session log rather than the device identity alone.

REQ-623|not-assessed.note: No adaptive authentication exists to test: the collector raises no trigger for a session opening outside the support window or from an address off the approved list, the gateway has no supplemental factor prompt in its build, and the circumstance list that would drive one has not been written as configuration.

REQ-624|pass.note: An escalation request inside an already authenticated session prompted for the full factor set again before it was granted, and a session idle by a second past the thirty minute mark required re-authentication before the next command was accepted. The memory scan taken after each trigger found no recoverable session key on the laptop, so a resumed session starts from a fresh grant rather than inheriting the earlier one.

REQ-625|pass.note: An arming command presented a second past the five minute window was rejected and the interlock stayed safe, and an attempt to satisfy the two-person rule with the same identity twice was rejected as well. A second arming command with no renewed re-authentication left the interface controller in the safe state, so the freshness of the authorisation is what releases the arming state rather than the fact that one was once given.

REQ-627|pass.note: No account in the controller table sits enabled without a sponsor authorisation record, and every record names a sponsor other than the applicant, so an account cannot be vouched for by the person who asked for it. Disabling an account left the authorisation record intact and retrievable, which is what lets a later review reconstruct who supported a privilege that has since been withdrawn.

REQ-631|pass.note: The policy and three of the five procedures carry a valid signature, a named approver and a recorded review date, the review-overdue report lists what has aged past twelve months, and a publication attempted from another endpoint was refused and recorded in the repository event log. The transport and sanitization-verification procedures are unsigned drafts and the media protection official's delegation is uncountersigned; both sit on the media-protection remediation list and were treated as open actions rather than as missing evidence.

REQ-632|pass.note: Four of the twelve check-out attempts came from identities absent from the custodian list and each was refused with no media serial released, the refusal reaching the collector inside sixty seconds in every case. Every cartridge held outside the library at the time of the test resolved to an open check-out record naming a current custodian, which follows from the storage module writing a cartridge only against an open record.

REQ-636|not-assessed.note: The review, approval, verification and disposal sequence runs today on a paper form with a wet signature; the record that would enforce the approver-not-operator rule and the presence of a verification result does not exist on the controller, so there was no system-held sequence for the custodian to walk through.

REQ-639|pass.note: A mass-storage device outside the signed allow-list did not enumerate as a storage volume on either maintenance port, while the port itself stayed electrically enabled for diagnostic use, and the refusal record naming the device serial and the port was retrievable inside sixty seconds. A write to an allow-listed device attempted from the mission computer in flight configuration failed and was recorded, so removable media on the platform is a read path only.

REQ-640|pass.note: Every entry in the portable-storage registry names a current custodian, an issue date and a device category, with vacancy state carried per entry, and the mount policy exported to both ground endpoints matched the registry as of its last publication timestamp. No mount record exists on either endpoint for a serial absent from the registry or marked vacant, so the no-identifiable-owner rule is enforced at mount rather than asserted in the procedure.
